skeleton:
Grilled Corn with Cumin

Moroccan · Easy · Serves 4

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The corn cart works the medina's edges from late summer through fall: whole ears turning over coals until the kernels blister in patches, then painted — painted, not buttered — with a wet salt rub and shaken in cumin. It is the simplest record on this site and among the most eaten: corn, fire, salt, cumin, and the paper napkin the street provides.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

Ingredients

  • the paint
- **Make the salt paint before the fire.** The salt water is the cart's tool: a brush or a folded paper towel dipped and dragged over the hot ear — it seasons in the steam and keeps the kernels from drying. The cumin goes in the paint (the even way) or dry in the shake (the loud way); the carts argue both. - **The bridge:** none — corn, salt, cumin. The fire is charcoal at its medium, or a gas flame, or the oven's broiler as the apartment's honest coal.

Grilled Corn with Cumin

Prep: 5 minutes · Cook: 15 minutes · Total: About 20 minutes · Serves 4

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 4 ears of corn (about 1 kg, or 250 g each), husked, or husked back and used as the handle
  • 2 tbsp coarse salt (about 20 g) dissolved in ¼ cup water (about 60 ml) — the paint
  • 2 tbsp ground cumin (about 8 g), either dusted dry or stirred into the salt paint; a lemon (about 80 g) beside
  • A pinch of chile flakes for the fierce register; a wedge of lime or lemon, optional but right

Instructions

  1. **Grill to blister (12–15 minutes).** Grill the ears over medium coals — turning every 3 minutes, patient through the kernels' slow color change from raw cream to cooked gold with dark blisters in patches — until the whole ear carries the char's perfume. Checkpoint — the target is patch, not blanket: kernels blistered dark in spots, gold-creamy between, the ear's sugars drawn to the surface. A uniformly black ear was rushed; a uniformly pale ear was never finished.
  2. **Paint and shake (1 minute, hot).** Straight off the grill: drag the salt paint over the hot ear — it hisses faintly and steams — then either roll the wet ear in the cumin or shake the cumin over from a height. The chile flakes ride the wet paint. Checkpoint — the ear should carry a wet shine that dries to a salt-crust glitter, the cumin clinging in the kernels' rows. Taste a kernel: salt first, cumin's earth, the char's smoke behind, the corn's own sweetness under all three — the quartet complete.
  3. **Serve in the husk-handle, hot.** Checkpoint — eating test: the kernels' snap between the teeth, blistered-sweet and salt-stung, cumin arriving at the swallow — a fierce, primitive, complete street food that needs nothing and gets it. The lime wedge, where run, is the modern city's addition, and the corn forgives it.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Corn burned blanket-blackCoals too fierceMedium coals, 3-minute turns
Kernels dry, leatheryUnder-painted or over-grilledThe salt paint during, not just after
Cumin fell to the plateApplied to a dry earPaint first \u2014 the wet carries the dry

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- Eaten in the ten minutes off the fire; the paint keeps a week in a jar. Leftover grilled corn's kernels cut off and fried next morning with the #19 kebda's spices is the street's own breakfast. - Variations: the chile-flecked fierce version, the lime modern register. The #30 chestnut cone is this record's fellow autumn cart on this site.
